## 13. Packs and rules: `supply-chain`

### supply-chain

Package sources and their verification (TLS, package indexes, vulnerability audits).

Detected by: a file matching `**/package.json`, `**/pyproject.toml`, `**/requirements*.txt`, `**/Pipfile`, `**/setup.py`, `**/Cargo.lock`.

| Rule | Description | Scope | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `supply-chain/audit-ignore-ratchet` | No new advisory ids (GHSA-…, CVE-…, PYSEC-…, RUSTSEC-…) in vulnerability-audit ignore lists (osv-scanner.toml, pnpm auditConfig, .nsprc, audit-ci, .trivyignore, .grype.yaml, --ignore-vuln in CI); a changed file may not have more than it had. Upgrade the dependency instead; ignoring an advisory is the user's decision: ask them. | any: `**/osv-scanner.toml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `**/package.json`, `.nsprc`, `audit-ci.json`, `audit-ci.jsonc`, `.trivyignore`, `.grype.yaml`, `.github/workflows/**`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `Makefile` | grep no-increase `(GHSA-[0-9a-z]{4}-[0-9a-z]{4}-[0-9a-z]{4}\|CVE-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{4,}\|PYSEC-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]+\|RUSTSEC-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{4})` |
| `supply-chain/insecure-download` | Claude asks before downloading without certificate checks (curl -k / --insecure, wget --no-check-certificate); fine for a local server with a self-signed certificate, not for anything fetched from the internet. | any | guard ask: command `{name: curl, flags_any: [-k, --insecure], value_flags: [-o, --output, -H, --header, -d, --data, --data-raw, --data-binary, -u, --user, -X, --request, -A, --user-agent, -e, --referer, -b, --cookie, -c, --cookie-jar, -T, --upload-file, -w, --write-out, -x, --proxy, -m, --max-time, --connect-timeout, -r, --range, -F, --form, --keepalive-time]}` or `{name: wget, flags_any: [--no-check-certificate]}` |
| `supply-chain/new-npm-dep-exists` | Each dependency a package.json gains (dependencies, devDependencies, optionalDependencies, peerDependencies; registry specs) exists on registry.npmjs.org, the newest version its range allows is not deprecated, and the package was first published at least 3 days ago; names a private registry serves (.npmrc @scope:registry=, or another default registry) are the registry's. | any: `**/package.json` | check lint: `forge_helper bun new_deps.mjs $FORGE_COOLDOWN_SECONDS` (when `**/package.json` changes) |
| `supply-chain/new-pypi-dep-exists` | Each dependency a pyproject.toml gains ([project] dependencies and optional-dependencies, [dependency-groups], [tool.uv] dev-dependencies, [tool.poetry.*dependencies]) exists on PyPI, has a release that is not yanked, and was first uploaded at least 3 days ago; names an explicit private index serves (uv sources, Poetry explicit sources) and path, git or URL sources are their own. | any: `**/pyproject.toml` | check lint: `forge_helper python new_deps.py $FORGE_COOLDOWN_SECONDS` (when `**/pyproject.toml` changes) |
| `supply-chain/no-dependency-confusion-command` | Claude asks before pip install with --extra-index-url or a uv command with an unsafe index strategy; a public package with an internal package's name would win. | any | guard ask: command `{name: [pip, pip3, pip3.*, uv], flags_any: [--extra-index-url]}` or `{name: [uv, uvx], option_values: {--index-strategy: ^unsafe-}}` |
| `supply-chain/no-dependency-confusion` | No pip --extra-index-url (requirements files, pip.conf / pip.ini, PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL, pip install in Dockerfiles, CI and scripts) and no uv index strategy unsafe-best-match or unsafe-first-match: pip merges every index and installs the highest version, so a public package with an internal package's name wins. Use one --index-url that proxies the public index, or uv indexes (first-index by default). | any: `**/requirements*.txt`, `**/constraints*.txt`, `**/pip.conf`, `**/pip.ini`, `@dockerfile`, `.github/workflows/**`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `**/*.sh`, `**/Makefile`, `**/tox.ini`, `**/noxfile.py`, `@env-template`, `**/pyproject.toml`, `**/uv.toml` | grep forbid `--extra-index-url\|PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL\|^[[:space:]]*extra-index-url[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]"'[]\|(index-strategy[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*["']\|UV_INDEX_STRATEGY=["']?\|--index-strategy[= ])unsafe-(best\|first)-match` |
| `supply-chain/no-tls-disable-command` | Commands never turn TLS verification off: no npm / pnpm / yarn config set strict-ssl false or --strict-ssl=false, NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0, PYTHONHTTPSVERIFY=0, GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY, git http.sslVerify false, pip --trusted-host / PIP_TRUSTED_HOST, uv --allow-insecure-host / UV_INSECURE_HOST. Every install would then accept an intercepted connection; install the proxy's CA certificate instead. | any | guard deny: command `{name: [npm, pnpm, yarn], sub: [config, set, strict-ssl, false]}` or `{name: [npm, pnpm, yarn], sub: [config, set, strict-ssl=false]}` or `{flags_any: [--strict-ssl=false, --allow-insecure-host, --trusted-host], value_flags: [--strict-ssl]}` or `{env_any: [GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY, PIP_TRUSTED_HOST, UV_INSECURE_HOST, NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0, PYTHONHTTPSVERIFY=0]}` or `{name: git, option_values: {-c: (?i)^http\.sslverify=(false\|0\|no\|off)$}}` or `{name: git, sub: [config, /(?i)^http\.sslverify$/, /(?i)^(false\|0\|no\|off)$/]}` or `{name: git, sub: [config, set, /(?i)^http\.sslverify$/, /(?i)^(false\|0\|no\|off)$/]}` |
| `supply-chain/no-tls-disable` | Committed files never turn TLS verification off: no strict-ssl=false (.npmrc), enableStrictSsl: false (.yarnrc.yml), NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0, PYTHONHTTPSVERIFY=0, sslVerify = false (git config), GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY, pip's --trusted-host / trusted-host =, uv's allow-insecure-host / UV_INSECURE_HOST. Install the proxy's CA certificate instead (NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, PIP_CERT, SSL_CERT_FILE). | any: `**`, `!**/*.{md,mdx,rst,adoc}`, `!**/README*`, `!**/CHANGELOG*`, `!**/docs/**`, `!**/doc/**` | grep forbid `strict-ssl[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*false\|enableStrictSsl:[[:space:]]*false\|NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED["']?[[:space:]]*[:=][[:space:]]*["']?0\|PYTHONHTTPSVERIFY["']?[[:space:]]*[:=][[:space:]]*["']?0\|sslVerify[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*false\|GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY\|--trusted-host\|^[[:space:]]*trusted-host[[:space:]]*=\|allow-insecure-host\|UV_INSECURE_HOST` |
| `supply-chain/vuln-audit` | A changed lock file brings in no dependency version with a known vulnerability (OSV, through osv-scanner) that its base version did not already have; osv-scanner.toml ignores do not apply. Needs api.osv.dev: offline, it is reported skipped. | any: `**/package-lock.json`, `**/pnpm-lock.yaml`, `**/yarn.lock`, `**/bun.lock`, `**/bun.lockb`, `**/uv.lock`, `**/poetry.lock`, `**/requirements*.txt`, `**/Pipfile.lock`, `**/pdm.lock`, `**/Cargo.lock` | check lint: `forge_osv` |
